repo.description: A high-performance framework for training LLMs, VLMs, diffusion, and embodied models on NVIDIA GPUs and Kunlun XPUs.  Supports  Pi0.5, GR00T-N1.7, FastWAM, Cosmos3, DreamZero, DeepSeek-V4,  GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3 and more.
repo.name: LoongForge

detail.body:
## Change Summary

**What changed?**

*Eval side (main)*
- `examples/embodied/fastwam/eval/configs/libero/*.yaml` (4 files): `sigma_shift` **5.0 -> 1.0** — the official action expert uses shift 1.0 and only the video expert stays at 5.0, while the old comment claimed 5.0 was the official value. Also declare `benchmark.prefer_controller_ee: false` (the official eval reads `obs['robot0_eef_pos']`; the runner defaults to the OSC controller cache) and `benchmark.controller_force_update: false`.
- `eval/orchestrator/runners/libero_runner.py`: new `--env-seed-mode {per_episode,per_task}` (`per_task` = the official semantics: one env per task, seeded once and reused across the 50 trials) and `--controller-force-update`; the runner now logs the effective value of both.
- `eval/orchestrator/config.py`: wire `benchmark.env_seed_mode` / `benchmark.controller_force_update` from the YAML into args.

*Training side (supporting)*
- `train/training_args.py`: new `--sampler-epoch-mode {advance,fixed}`, plus the new module `data/datasets/fastwam/samplers.py`. `fixed` pins the epoch to 0 to reproduce standalone FastWAM's `ResumableEpochSampler`, whose epoch never advances so every epoch reuses one permutation. The default `advance` keeps the existing behaviour bit-identical.
- New `configs/models/embodied/fastwam_aligned.yaml` / `fastwam_aligned_accel.yaml` and `examples/embodied/fastwam/run_fastwam_sft_ddp_zero1_finetune_official_aligned.sh` package the "training-side alignment + acceleration" recipe as a one-shot reproduction.

*Small boundary fix on top of #269*
- `data/datasets/lerobot_dataset.py`: `MultiLeRobotV2Dataset(roots=[])` used to build a silent zero-length dataset (the sampler yields nothing and training does no work). It now raises `ValueError` in the constructor.

**Which issue or requirement does this address?**
While reproducing FastWAM with LoongForge we found several places where the eval protocol disagreed with the official harness (most importantly `sigma_shift`, worth ~3pt). This PR aligns the eval side item by item and packages the aligned training recipe as an example, so that the same weights evaluated in both frameworks agree (TOTAL differs by <= 0.4pt).

**Which modules are affected?**
`loongforge/embodied/eval/` (orchestrator + LIBERO runner), `loongforge/embodied/train/` (training_args), `loongforge/embodied/data/datasets/` (new sampler, lerobot_dataset guard), `examples/embodied/fastwam/`, `configs/models/embodied/`.

## Validation

- [x] I ran the relevant local checks.
  `python3 -m py_compile` on the changed files, `yaml.safe_load` on all 4 + 2 configs, `bash -n` on the new script, and `python3 ci/sensitive_scan.py` (**0 errors**).
- [ ] I added or updated tests where appropriate.
  No new tests: the change is config + opt-in flags, and the default behaviour for every other model is unchanged bit-for-bit (see below). Happy to add unit tests for `MultiLeRobotV2Dataset(roots=[])` raising and for the `--sampler-epoch-mode=fixed` wrapper if wanted.
- [x] I checked compatibility with existing APIs and configurations.
  All new flags are opt-in. `libero_runner`'s three defaults stay legacy (`controller_force_update=True`, `env_seed_mode=per_episode`, `prefer_controller_ee=True`), so **LIBERO evaluation for every other model is unchanged**; only the FastWAM configs opt out explicitly.

**End-to-end run (8x A800, full 2000 episodes)**

Retrained on this branch and evaluated in full, paired episode-by-episode against the pre-rebase branch (same recipe):

| suite | this branch | before | delta | McNemar p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| libero_10 | 471/500 = **94.20%** | 463/500 = 92.60% | +1.60 | 0.291 |
| spatial | 485/500 = **97.00%** | 488/500 = 97.60% | -0.60 | 0.677 |
| object | 498/500 = **99.60%** | 497/500 = 99.40% | +0.20 | 1.000 |
| goal | 486/500 = **97.20%** | 485/500 = 97.00% | +0.20 | 1.000 |
| **TOTAL** | 1940/2000 = **97.00%** | 1933/2000 = 96.65% | +0.35 | -- |

- Training: `fp32 master + accel` recipe, 20k steps, **~1405 ms/step**, no NaN / no skipped iterations; final loss matches the previous run (video 0.07669 vs 0.07690).
- Eval protocol: `noise_seed=42`, `run.seed=42` + `per_task`, `sigma_shift=1.0`, `prefer_controller_ee=false`, `controller_force_update=false`, official `max_steps` (700|400), 50 trials/task.
- Every per-suite difference is **statistically insignificant** (p >= 0.29) -> no regression.

## CI, GPU, and Image Impact

- [ ] This change affects dependencies, Dockerfiles, patches, or runtime environments.
- [x] GPU validation is required. Suggested suite: `embodied`.
      We already ran the full thing locally on 8x A800 (20k training + 4 suites x 500 episodes); a smoke run over the `embodied` eval path in CI is recommended.
- [ ] A local candidate image should be built during GPU validation.
- [ ] No GPU or image validation is required.

## Reviewer Notes

**Known risks / trade-offs**
1. **`libero_runner`'s defaults are deliberately kept legacy.** `--controller-force-update` defaults to `True` (the pre-change behaviour) because the runner is shared by *every* model evaluated on LIBERO, and flipping the default would silently change their first observation. The four FastWAM configs set it to `false` explicitly to match the official eval.
2. **The two new configs carry placeholder machine-specific paths** (`norm_stats_path: /path/to/dataset_stats.json`, `tokenizer_model_id: /path/to/...`); users must fill them in.
3. **The empty-roots guard in `MultiLeRobotV2Dataset`** is a follow-up to the just-merged #269. It is added in the constructor only (there is a single caller, and the message is enough to locate it).

**Note on evaluation variance (for future comparisons)**
Retraining with identical code, data and recipe yields weights whose loss differs by ~0.2%; on `libero_10` that amplifies to **+/-1.6pt** (the evaluation itself is deterministic: rerunning the same weights reproduces all 500 episodes bit-for-bit). So **a single `libero_10` number is not a criterion**; compare changes on `spatial/object/goal` (delta <= 0.6pt here) together with a McNemar test. This matches public practice (the LeRobot docs recommend averaging over >=3 seeds; a 500-episode suite carries a ~+/-2-4pt confidence interval).

**Follow-ups (not in this PR)**
- RoboTwin-side alignment (launch script + `camera_layout` + the `z-score` alias in `normalizer`) is held back until the RoboTwin alignment settles.
- To reduce evaluation variance further, training can be made deterministic (disable `cudnn.benchmark`, enable `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms`) at some throughput cost.

@@ -0,0 +1,153 @@
+# Copyright 2026 The LoongForge Authors.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""FastWAM sampler registry hook.
+
+FastWAM has no bespoke index ordering, so the *default* path is reused verbatim
+(``default_sampler_builder``): with the default ``--distributed-sampler-mode=cyclic``
+that is ``torchdata.StatefulDistributedSampler``, whose permutation is
+``randperm(seed + epoch)`` and therefore reshuffles every epoch.
+
+This module exists to make that epoch behaviour *controllable*, because standalone
+FastWAM (the reference implementation we reproduce) never advances its sampler
+epoch: ``ResumableEpochSampler.__iter__`` seeds with
+``seed + self.epoch + self.epoch_offset``, and the only caller of
+``set_epoch_offset`` is its resume path -- so during normal training the seed stays
+``seed`` and **every epoch reuses the same permutation**. ``--sampler-epoch-mode=fixed``
+reproduces that.
+
+Why a registered builder instead of patching the default one: the failure mode this
+replaces was a switch written into the *wrong* sampler class, which silently did
+nothing. FastWAM receives ``StatefulDistributedSampler`` (not ``_BlockShardSampler``)
+because ``default_sampler_builder`` branches on ``distributed_sampler_mode``, whose
+default is ``"cyclic"``. Registering here bypasses that branch entirely, so the knob
+provably applies to the class actually in use.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import itertools
+import os
+from typing import Any, Iterator
+
+from torch.utils.data import Sampler
+
+from loongforge.embodied.data.datasets.sampler_builder import (
+    SamplerBuilderContext,
+    default_sampler_builder,
+    register_sampler_builder,
+)
+
+# Announced (pid, class, mode) triples, so the construction line is printed once.
+_ANNOUNCED: set = set()
+
+# Epoch fingerprints already printed, so a pinned epoch prints once per process
+# (that repetition is itself the evidence the order is fixed).
+_FINGERPRINTS: set = set()
+
+_FINGERPRINT_LEN = 256
+
+
+def _fingerprint(sampler: Sampler) -> str:
+    """Short digest of the permutation this sampler would yield now."""
+    head = list(itertools.islice(iter(sampler), _FINGERPRINT_LEN))
+    return hashlib.sha1(",".join(map(str, head)).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
+
+
+def _order_audit(sampler: Sampler) -> None:
+    """Print a fingerprint of the current permutation, once per (pid, epoch).
+
+    With the epoch pinned (mode=fixed) every iteration yields the same digest and
+    this prints exactly once -- i.e. the training log itself proves the sampling
+    order did not change. With mode=advance it prints one differing line per epoch.
+    """
+    epoch = getattr(sampler, "epoch", None)
+    key = (os.getpid(), type(sampler).__name__, str(epoch))
+    if key in _FINGERPRINTS:
+        return
+    _FINGERPRINTS.add(key)
+    print(
+        f"[fastwam-sampler] order epoch={epoch} sampler={type(sampler).__name__} "
+        f"seed={getattr(sampler, 'seed', None)} rank={getattr(sampler, 'rank', None)}"
+        f"/{getattr(sampler, 'num_replicas', None)} order_sha1={_fingerprint(sampler)}",
+        flush=True,
+    )
+
+
+class _FixedEpochSampler(Sampler[int]):
+    """Pin ``inner``'s epoch to 0 so every epoch reuses one permutation.
+
+    Wraps rather than subclasses because the concrete class is chosen by
+    ``default_sampler_builder`` (``StatefulDistributedSampler`` for the default
+    ``cyclic`` mode, ``_BlockShardSampler`` for ``block``). The stateful API is
+    delegated explicitly: ``StatefulDataLoader`` persists the sampler via
+    ``state_dict`` / ``load_state_dict``, and dropping that would silently break
+    in-epoch resume.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, inner: Sampler[int]) -> None:
+        self._inner = inner
+        if hasattr(inner, "set_epoch"):
+            inner.set_epoch(0)
+
+    def set_epoch(self, epoch: int) -> None:  # noqa: ARG002 - epoch intentionally ignored
+        """Ignore the trainer's epoch advance and keep the inner sampler at 0."""
+        if hasattr(self._inner, "set_epoch"):
+            self._inner.set_epoch(0)
+
+    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[int]:
+        _order_audit(self._inner)
+        return iter(self._inner)
+
+    def __len__(self) -> int:
+        return len(self._inner)
+
+    def state_dict(self) -> Any:
+        """Delegate stateful resume to the wrapped sampler."""
+        return self._inner.state_dict()
+
+    def load_state_dict(self, state_dict: Any) -> None:
+        """Delegate stateful resume to the wrapped sampler."""
+        self._inner.load_state_dict(state_dict)
+
+    def __getattr__(self, item: str) -> Any:
+        # Anything else StatefulDataLoader / the trainer may look up.
+        return getattr(self.__dict__["_inner"], item)
+
+

inline_comments.body:
This inherits `--clip-grad 1.0` from the base script, but official FastWAM effectively runs **without** gradient clipping:

1. [`configs/train.yaml#L30`](https://github.com/yuantianyuan01/FastWAM/blob/main/configs/train.yaml#L30) sets `max_grad_norm: 1.0`, and [`trainer.py#L701`](https://github.com/yuantianyuan01/FastWAM/blob/main/src/fastwam/trainer.py#L701) calls `accelerator.clip_grad_norm_(...)`.
2. Training runs under DeepSpeed ([`accelerate_zero1_ds.yaml`](https://github.com/yuantianyuan01/FastWAM/blob/main/scripts/accelerate_configs/accelerate_zero1_ds.yaml)). In that mode `Accelerator.clip_grad_norm_` only returns `engine.get_global_grad_norm()` and ignores `max_norm`; clipping is delegated to DeepSpeed's `gradient_clipping`.
3. [`ds_zero1_config.json`](https://github.com/yuantianyuan01/FastWAM/blob/main/scripts/ds_configs/ds_zero1_config.json) has no `gradient_clipping` key, and DeepSpeed's `GRADIENT_CLIPPING_DEFAULT = 0.` (`deepspeed/runtime/constants.py`). Accelerate's `gradient_clipping: 1.0` kwarg only fills keys set to `"auto"`, so it isn't injected either.

We verified this on the real FastWAM trainer (8 GPUs): `clip_grad=0.0` at runtime, step-1 global grad norm ≈ 19.6, unchanged after the clip call. LF only matched FW bit-for-bit after switching to `--clip-grad 0`.

Since grad norms are ~20–130, `--clip-grad 1.0` fires on every step in LF. Under Adam a per-step global rescale mostly cancels out, which is probably why eval still lands within noise. But it does reweight steps in the moment estimates and is one source of the residual you measured. Please use `--clip-grad 0`.

+export DATASET_PATH=${DATASET_PATH:-"$DIFFSYNTH_MODEL_BASE_PATH/LIBERO-fastwam/libero_spatial_no_noops_lerobot,$DIFFSYNTH_MODEL_BASE_PATH/LIBERO-fastwam/libero_object_no_noops_lerobot,$DIFFSYNTH_MODEL_BASE_PATH/LIBERO-fastwam/libero_goal_no_noops_lerobot,$DIFFSYNTH_MODEL_BASE_PATH/LIBERO-fastwam/libero_10_no_noops_lerobot"}
+export ACTION_DIT_PRETRAINED_PATH=${ACTION_DIT_PRETRAINED_PATH:-"$DIFFSYNTH_MODEL_BASE_PATH/checkpoints/ActionDiT_linear_interp_Wan22_alphascale_1024hdim.pt"}
+export TEXT_EMBEDDING_CACHE_DIR=${TEXT_EMBEDDING_CACHE_DIR:-"$DIFFSYNTH_MODEL_BASE_PATH/data/text_embeds_cache/libero"}
+export OUTPUT_DIR=${OUTPUT_DIR:-"$LOONGFORGE_PATH/outputs/fastwam_sft_official_aligned"}
+export TRAIN_ITERS=${TRAIN_ITERS:-20000}
+export GPUS_PER_NODE=${GPUS_PER_NODE:-8}
+export SEED=${SEED:-42}
+
+# Official-aligned YAML (model: + data: sections). --model-name (set by the base
+# script, default "fastwam") is still required: it selects the ModelConfig /
+# DataConfig classes.
+CONFIG_FILE=${CONFIG_FILE:-"$LOONGFORGE_PATH/configs/models/embodied/fastwam_aligned.yaml"}
+if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
+    echo "ERROR: aligned config not found: $CONFIG_FILE" >&2
+    exit 1
+fi
+
+# Pin the sampler epoch to 0: standalone FastWAM's ResumableEpochSampler seeds with
+# `seed + epoch + epoch_offset` and never advances the epoch during normal training,
+# so every epoch reuses ONE permutation. Set SAMPLER_EPOCH_MODE=advance to restore
+# LoongForge's per-epoch reshuffle.
+SAMPLER_EPOCH_MODE=${SAMPLER_EPOCH_MODE:-fixed}
+
+# Plain AdamW (no `fused` kwarg) = official's code path. "TorchFusedAdamW" is the same
+# class with fused=True, which is a different CUDA kernel. See the header note.
+OPTIMIZER=${OPTIMIZER:-AdamW}
+
+echo "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
+echo "  LoongForge FastWAM SFT (OFFICIAL-ALIGNED, 4-suite joint)"
+echo "  Config:    $CONFIG_FILE"
+echo "  Data:      $DATASET_PATH"
+echo "  Output:    $OUTPUT_DIR"
+echo "  Iters:     $TRAIN_ITERS   GPUs: $GPUS_PER_NODE   Seed: $SEED"
+echo "  Sampler:   epoch-mode=$SAMPLER_EPOCH_MODE"
+echo "  Optimizer: $OPTIMIZER"
+echo "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
+
+# NOTE: "$@" is appended AFTER the optionals below. Flags are safe there (a repeated
+# flag simply wins, e.g. --sampler-epoch-mode advance). Bare dotlist overrides are
+# NOT: argparse's positional `overrides` (nargs="*") fails with "unrecognized
+# arguments" when it appears after an optional that takes a value.
+bash "$LOONGFORGE_PATH/examples/embodied/fastwam/run_fastwam_sft_ddp_zero1_finetune.sh" \
+    --config-file "$CONFIG_FILE" \
+    --optimizer "$OPTIMIZER" \
+    --lr-base 1e-4 --lr-warmup-iters 1000 --min-lr 1e-6 \
+    --sampler-epoch-mode "$SAMPLER_EPOCH_MODE" \
+    "$@"

@XueSongTap 
**1. `--clip-grad` (line 158)** — mechanism confirmed as you described. Only the magnitude needs correcting: that value goes to wandb only (`wandb.enabled: false`), so we instrumented the real trainer (8xA800, 4-suite LIBERO, 300 steps):

```
official: min 0.283  max 7.098  mean 1.238  median 0.916  (>1.0 on 43.7%)
step 1: 7.098465 (official)  vs  7.093750 (LF)
```

~0.3–7.1, not 20–130, and it is the same quantity on both sides (step 1 agrees to 0.07%).

Cost of removing the clip (20k SFT + 2000 eval episodes, only `--clip-grad` changed):

| suite | clip=1.0 | clip=0 | Δ | McNemar p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| libero_10 | 471/500 = 94.20% | 454/500 = 90.80% | −3.40pt | 0.020 |
| spatial | 485/500 = 97.00% | 487/500 = 97.40% | +0.40pt | 0.814 |
| object | 498/500 = 99.60% | 498/500 = 99.60% | 0.00pt | 0.617 |
| goal | 486/500 = 97.20% | 488/500 = 97.60% | +0.40pt | 0.831 |
| **TOTAL** | 1940/2000 = **97.00%** | 1927/2000 = **96.35%** | **−0.65pt** | — |

Only libero_10 is affected. Default stays at LF's 1.0; `CLIP_GRAD=0` gives exact parity.

**2. Line 20** — fixed. The class default is already 1.0/1.0 (#240); 5.0 is the video scheduler.

**3. Line 1** — folded. Doing it exposed a real drift: the wrapper never passed `--lr-decay-style`, so it ran `cosine_warmup_with_min_lr` instead of the validated `linear_warmup_cosine_annealing`.
- `run_fastwam_sft_ddp_zero1_finetune.sh` now takes env knobs (`LR_DECAY_STYLE`/`OPTIMIZER`/`CLIP_GRAD`/`SAMPLER_EPOCH_MODE`/`ZERO_MASTER_PARAM_DTYPE`/`SAVE_FORMAT`/`ASYNC_SAVE`) + `EXTRA_MODEL_OVERRIDES`/`EXTRA_DATA_OVERRIDES` dotlist hatches; recipe in the header. Opt-in flags are only added when set, so an unset invocation's argv is byte-identical (verified with a stub `torchrun`), and the dotlist form resolves to the same model/data config the YAML had (verified).
- Deleted the wrapper and both `fastwam_aligned*.yaml`.

**4.** Also trimmed the repeated comments in the four LIBERO eval configs. Note the eval-side `sigma_shift` default was already 1.0 — the bug was only the YAML's explicit 5.0.
@yuehang-sun1998 Fine to keep `--clip-grad 1.0` as the LF default.
